result.topic_en: Summing cos φ + cos 2φ + … + cos 8φ by a telescoping sine identity to get −1/2, then forming products of partial sums of cosines and the resulting quadratic for e and f, as in the division of the circle into 17 parts.
result.transcription:
cf. Lagrange[?] n. 518

$\Sigma = (\cos\varphi + \cos 2\varphi + \dots \cos 8\varphi)$

$\sin(\varphi+\frac12\varphi) - \sin(\varphi-\frac12\varphi) = 2\sin\frac12\varphi\cos\varphi$
$\sin(\varphi+\frac32\varphi) - \sin(\varphi+\frac12\varphi) = 2\sin\frac12\varphi\cos 2\varphi$
$\sin(\varphi+\frac52\varphi) - \sin(\varphi+\frac32\varphi) = 2\sin\frac12\varphi\cos 3\varphi$
$\sin(\varphi+\frac72\varphi) - \sin(\varphi+\frac52\varphi) = 2\sin\frac12\varphi\cos 4\varphi$
$\vdots$
$\sin(\varphi+\frac{13}{2}\varphi) - \sin(\varphi+\frac{11}{2}\varphi) = 2\sin\frac12\varphi\cos 7\varphi$
$\sin(\varphi+\frac{15}{2}\varphi) - \sin(\varphi+\frac{13}{2}\varphi) = 2\sin\frac12\varphi\cos 8\varphi$

$\Sigma = \frac{\sin(\varphi+\frac{15}{2}\varphi) - \sin(\varphi-\frac12\varphi)}{2\sin\frac12\varphi} = $ [-...-] $\frac{\sin\frac{17}{2}\varphi - \sin\frac12\varphi}{2\sin\frac12\varphi} = \frac{\sin 180^\circ - \sin\frac12\varphi}{2\sin\frac12\varphi} = -\frac12$

[-ab-] $2ab = 2\cos\varphi\cos 2\varphi + 2\cos\varphi\cos 8\varphi + 2\cos 4\varphi\cos 2\varphi + 2\cos 4\varphi\cos 8\varphi$
[-...-]
$= \cos\varphi + \cos 3\varphi + \cos 8\varphi + \cos 7\varphi + \cos 6\varphi + \cos 2\varphi + \cos 5\varphi + \cos 4\varphi = e+f.$

ab/c[?] $2ac = 2\cos\varphi\cos 3\varphi + \cos\varphi\cos 5\varphi + \cos 4\varphi\cos 3\varphi + \cos 4\varphi\cos 5\varphi$
[-...-]
$= \cos 4\varphi + \cos 2\varphi + \cos 6\varphi + \cos 4\varphi + \cos 7\varphi + \cos\varphi + \cos 8\varphi + \cos\varphi = $ [-...-] $2a+b+d.$

$2bc$ 2[-...-] $= a + 2c + d$
$2ad$ = [?] $= b + 2d + c$
$2ac$. 2[?] $= 2a + b + d$
$2cd$ $2bd = e+f$

$0 = (x-e)(x-f) = x^2 - (e+f)x + ef = 0$
also[?] $e+f = -\frac12$ $\quad e^2 - 1 = -\frac12 e$
$ef = -1$ $\quad e^2 + \frac12 e = 1$
$e^2 + \frac12 e + \frac1{16} = \frac{17}{16}$
$e = -\frac14 \pm \sqrt{\frac{17}{16}}.$

methods.what: Telescoping identity sin(x+½φ) − sin(x−½φ) = 2 sin ½φ cos x, used to sum consecutive cosines
Sum of cos kφ for k = 1 to 8 equals −1/2 when 17φ/2 = 180°
Product of the partial sums a and b, reduced by product-to-sum formulas, gives the sum of all eight cosines
Product of the partial sums a and c expressed linearly in the partial sums
Table of the products of the partial sums a, b, c, d as linear combinations of them
e and f are the roots of a quadratic with e+f = −1/2 and ef = −1, solved by completing the square
